Reading time now lands on the day you actually read it.

### Fixed

* **"Today" could show 0 minutes after a long read, while another day got too much.** The Kindle only keeps a running total per book, with no dates. InkSights used to split the time between two launches using the book's "page history" timestamps, but those turned out to record only jumps (following a link, Go To), not reading. Most books have none, so all the time went on the day you opened InkSights; books with a jump put it all on that jump's day.

### New

* **Wake/sleep recorder.** A tiny background script (`activity.sh`) logs when the Kindle wakes and sleeps, and which book is open when it sleeps, to `reading-stats/activity.log`. Time read between launches is split across days by how long the screen was on each day. Time asleep in a different book doesn't count. The recorder starts the first time you open InkSights after a restart and sits idle between events.
* **Uses CoverSleep's log too**, if you have [CoverSleep](https://github.com/dq-stack/CoverSleep), for any stretch the recorder wasn't running (for example before you installed this version).
* **`tools/redate-history.py`** (in the source, runs on a computer) re-splits an existing reading log by day from a USB-mounted Kindle's wake/sleep logs. Totals don't change. Dry run by default; `--write` saves it and keeps a backup.

### Downloads

* `inksights-1.2.0.zip`: the Kindle app
* `inksights-backup-calibre-1.2.0.zip`: the optional calibre backup plugin (unchanged; it now also backs up `activity.log` as part of `reading-stats/`)

### Upgrading from v1.1.x

Copy the new `extensions` and `documents` folders over the old ones, then open InkSights once to start the recorder. Your reading log in `reading-stats/` is kept. Reading done before the upgrade keeps its old day split unless you run `tools/redate-history.py`.
